title: Multi-Discipline Ops Brief — 2026-08-12
content:
Attendees: Aisha (chair), Marcus, Elena, Samir, Priya, Jonah (SRE), Mei (Serving Runtime lead), Luis (Private Deployments PM), two notes: Veronica, Ken (excused)

Objective: Weekly cross-team leadership alignment focusing on short-term capacity plan for Hosted/Dedicated, Private deployment onboarding checklist, a quick postmortem follow-up on the 2026-08-08 capacity spike, and a lightweight decision on next week's release window. Goal: clear actionable owners and deconflict any cross-team rollout that could impact SLOs.

Agenda:
- Quick metrics and capacity snapshot
- Incident recap & follow-ups (8/8 spike)
- Dedicated capacity rollouts: staging -> canary -> prod schedule
- Private customer onboarding readiness checklist
- Release freeze proposal for minor infra changes
- Open questions / risks / blockers

1) Metrics / snapshot (Jonah)
- Current 7d avg p99 latency (hosted text generation): 480ms (target SLA 450ms) — trending +8% week-over-week
- Active serving nodes allocated to hosted pool: 116 (target planned ramp for month-end: 140)
- Dedicated reserved capacity utilization: 72% avg (some customers spiking to 95% during regional lab tests)
- KV cache hit-rate: 18% (improvement plan in Optimize backlog)

Notes: latency bump correlated with two customers' long-sequence tests and a config drift causing smaller batch sizes in the serving runtime. Jonah to provide per-route breakdown by EOD Monday.

2) 8/8 capacity spike postmortem highlights (Mei + SRE)
- Root cause: simultaneous long-context inference jobs from two sandbox accounts routed to same GPU cluster because routing rules failed to fallback to lower-cost variants when quota-throttled.
- Contributing factors: missing guardrails on per-account long-seq limits for hosted tier; recent routing policy change (INF-4123) had a regression in the compatible-variant map.
- Immediate mitigations taken: temporary soft-quota on long-seq requests for sandbox accounts; manual redistribution of jobs across clusters.

Decisions:
- Add emergency rule to routing layer to force-evict long-sequence sandbox jobs to a low-priority burst pool when cluster utilization > 85% (owner: Mei, due: 2026-08-14).
- Create short-term dashboard for ‘long-seq request’ counts by account and cluster (owner: Jonah + Observability, due: 2026-08-16).

Action items from postmortem:
- Mei: implement routing layer guard (PR + test) and schedule canary (due 2026-08-14) — status: in_progress
- Samir (Infra): provision a 12-node low-priority burst pool for sandbox (due 2026-08-15) — status: open
- Aisha: draft customer communication template for affected sandbox users (due 2026-08-13) — status: open

3) Dedicated rollout schedule reality check (Luis + Platform Eng)
- Current plan: staging -> canary (5% traffic) -> regional ramp -> global prod; target start for canary: 2026-08-18.
- Observations: Platform tests show 9% higher token-cost on the new kernel profile for medium context; Finance raised concern about cost delta on customer billing if we switch without opt-in.

Decision and constraints:
- Proceed with canary on 8/18 but limit to internal and opt-in customers only; do not flip default model variant until after cost-evaluation window (2 weeks). Owner: Luis to confirm canary cohort list by 2026-08-13.

Action items:
- Luis: confirm opt-in cohort, create communication plan (due 2026-08-13)
- Finance (Elena): run token-cost projection against historical 90-day workloads and publish a recommendation (due 2026-08-17)

4) Private Deployments onboarding checklist review (Priya + Solutions Eng)
- Checklist draft items reviewed: infra checklist, KMS/HSM integration steps, audit-log collection, network egress policies, on-prem install runbook, SLA terms.
- Major missing piece: automated verification that customer-provided nodes meet GPU capability matrix (driver + cuDNN + kernel versions). Risk: on-site time for driver fixes adds 3–4 days to onboarding.

Decision: build a small 'env-checker' tool (CLI) to validate node stack pre-onboarding. Owner: Solutions Eng (Priya) + Eng-Release (Samir) to scope. Deliverable: MVP CLI + docs (due 2026-08-30).

Action items:
- Priya: scope env-checker features and sample output; sketch integration with installer (due 2026-08-16).
- Samir: add test harness to release CI to run env-checker on infra lab nodes (due 2026-08-23).

5) Release window / freeze proposal (Aisha)
- Proposal: soft-freeze for minor infra changes for 2026-08-17 through 2026-08-20 (one week overlap with canary) to avoid compounding changes during canary ramp. Emergency fixes allowed with explicit approval from leads.
- Rationale: reduce risk surface while canary is evaluated; recent incidents show small infra changes can shift batching behavior.

Decision: APPROVED soft-freeze. Leads to maintain a pre-approved emergency list. Owner: Aisha to publish policy and emergency contact list (due 2026-08-13).

6) Hiring / resourcing flags (Marcus)
- Open reqs for SRE (2), Serving Runtime engineer (1), Solutions Eng (1). Recruiting pipeline slow; target to accelerate interviews for SRE role by reallocating two hiring panel members from Platform.

Action: Marcus to propose panel schedule and ask Eng managers to prioritize interviews (due 2026-08-14).

7) Cross-team blockers and asks
- Observability: need tag standardization (route/model/customer) across teams for reliable cost attribution — ask: product + runtime agree on tag list (owner: Elena + Mei) due 2026-08-19.
- Console: rollout of per-route cost UI delayed by two sprints due to API changes (Console team). Impact: customers won't see per-route delta during canary. Risk accepted for now; mitigate with manual reports.

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Should we automatically downgrade long-seq requests to a lower-precision variant when cluster load high, or only evict? Tradeoffs: quality regressions vs. availability. Next discussion: tech deep-dive 2026-08-16 (Mei to lead).
- Billing behavior for dedicated customers during kernel-profile switch: do we apply retroactive credits if cost exceeds estimates? Finance to recommend policy by 2026-08-17.

Loose brainstorm notes (informal):
- Idea: temporary "sandbox tier" with strict long-seq caps and cheaper pricing; could be useful for experimenters but needs billing plumbing.
- Suggestion: run synthetic long-seq soak test nightly against a dedicated low-priority pool to detect regressions early. (Jonah to prototype)
- TODO: collect a handful of customer workload traces for cost-projection (ask Solutions Eng + CS).

Quick metrics scoreboard (snapshot at meeting):
- Hosted p99: 480ms (450ms target)
- Hosted p50: 120ms
- KV cache hit rate: 18%
- Dedicated utilization: 72%
- Sandbox long-seq count (24h): 1,420 requests

Meeting close: next cross-team check-in: 2026-08-16 (technical deep-dive on long-seq fallback and downgrade approach). Aisha to circulate notes + action list.

Owners recap (single-line):
- Mei: routing guard PR + canary (due 2026-08-14)
- Jonah: long-seq dashboard (due 2026-08-16)
- Samir: sandbox burst pool + CI test harness (due 2026-08-15 & 2026-08-23)
- Luis: canary cohort confirmation + comms (due 2026-08-13)
- Elena: finance token-cost projection (due 2026-08-17)
- Priya: env-checker scope (due 2026-08-16)
- Marcus: hiring panel schedule (due 2026-08-14)
- Aisha: publish release soft-freeze policy & customer comms (due 2026-08-13)

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Add links to dashboards in Confluence page (Aisha)
- Confirm legal sign-off window for private onboarding contract template (Priya)
- Revisit canary cohort after first 48h and re-evaluate risk posture

End of notes.
